A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TT-Occ, despite the changed title and presentation. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original TT-Occ benchmark results, component and TRBF ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, RayIoU comparisons, foundation-model ablations, memory measurements, and rainy/nighttime evaluations.

M1.justification: v3 integrates GroundedSAM2 and REX-Omni semantic alternatives and a MapAnything geometry variant that uses metric depth directly, bypassing VGGT's triangulation calibration. These are component-level adaptations; the Gaussian representation, tracking strategies, TRBF smoothing, and voxelization procedure remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Occ3D-nuScenes and nuCraft remain the benchmark datasets. v3 adds explicitly evaluated rainy and nighttime scenarios in Appendix B.1, while removing v2's six-step demonstration of introducing new semantic queries during a sequence (Figure 5).

E2.justification: The occupancy-accuracy comparator sets in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged. However, the computational-cost comparison narrows: v3 Figure 1 omits BEVFormer, CTF-Occ, and RenderOcc, whose pretraining costs appeared alongside TT-Occ in v2 Table 1.

E3.justification: v3 adds RayIoU@1/2/4 comparisons controlled to use OpenSeeD, evaluates additional semantic/depth configurations, and specifies five adverse-condition scenes. The appendix also replaces the earlier semantic query list with a shorter list including barrier and trailer. Main validation coverage, voxel resolutions, spatial ranges, and stated mIoU class exclusions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands analysis through semantic/depth-model sensitivity tests and rainy/nighttime robustness evaluations. Conversely, it removes the open-vocabulary sequence case study, the quantitative TRBF ablation, and the resolution-dependent FPS comparison. The original A-D component ablations and qualitative TRBF demonstration are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed variability, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The added averages and result rows do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Camera/LiDAR mIoU changes from 13.43/23.60 to 16.70/27.41 in Table 1 and from 4.33/9.08 to 5.95/10.92 in Table 2. v3 Table 4 associates the new Occ3D scores with stronger VFM configurations, preventing interpretation as unchanged-setting gains. SelfOcc's Table 1 mIoU changes from 9.30 to 10.54 despite unchanged class scores. RayIoU, VFM, memory, and weather results are added; quantitative TRBF and nuCraft FPS entries are removed.

T1.justification: The Gaussian, TRBF, and voxelization mathematics in Equations 1-6 are retained. Added camera subscripts and explanations around Equation 2 clarify existing notation. No substantive new assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of occupancy prediction without task-specific network training, flexible voxel resolutions, open-vocabulary recognition, temporal coherence, and competitive accuracy and efficiency. The additional experiments support these existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting RayIoU to geometric accuracy, MapAnything's advantage to metric-depth calibration, and adverse-condition performance to foundation-model generalization. It also explains memory bottlenecks. The earlier OpenSeeD category-mismatch limitation and resolution-scaling runtime explanation disappear, while camera/LiDAR geometry limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents additional VFM configurations, revised semantic prompts, Gaussian counts, and peak memory, and clarifies that the 10% ablation subset is held-out validation data. It removes the explicit full-resolution OpenSeeD input statement and v2's prospective code-release URL; this establishes a disclosure change, not actual repository availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for REX-Omni, MapAnything, Grounded SAM, Flash3D, AutoOcc, and the RayIoU-related sparse panoptic occupancy work, while dropping the PatchWork++ reference. The principal positioning against offline-trained occupancy predictors and scene-reconstruction methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and author line change, VLM terminology becomes VFM, and the introduction, conclusion, and selected explanations are revised. References move before a separately organized supplement. Most method prose and the main section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The paper switches from a single-column to a two-column layout and substantially redesigns its visual presentation. v3 introduces a cost-accuracy plot and detailed pipeline diagram, combines component tables with ablation images, converts timing tables to a stacked chart, and reorganizes qualitative comparisons and appendix figures.

improvement.justification: The controlled RayIoU comparison, VFM component tests, adverse-condition evaluations, and memory measurements strengthen support for modularity, geometric quality, and practical feasibility. These gains are limited by removal of the open-vocabulary case study and quantitative TRBF evidence, reduced implementation disclosure, and unreconciled SelfOcc summaries: 10.54 in Table 1 versus 11.6 in Table 4. Overall, the expanded validation provides a limited net improvement.
